status: Proposal for community discussion. The whitepaper (6.3) commits to standard, machine-readable reason codes and names six of them; this registry is a candidate concrete list plus a governance model for it. The policy notes below are proposals, not settled positions.

policy.additivity: PROPOSED: codes are deprecated, never removed or renumbered, so that a code recorded today still resolves when read back later.
policy.wire_granularity: PROPOSED: the code returned at check time stays coarse, since detailed codes can leak rule structure and, in sanctions cases, disclosure may itself be restricted. UNSPECIFIED_DENY exists for cases where even a category is too revealing.
open_questions: Who governs additions to this registry?
Is a coarse wire code plus a separate detailed path the right split, and what carries the detailed path?
Must a code recorded in a later compliance record be the identical token to the one returned at check time?

codes.description: Offering-level holder cap would be exceeded.

codes.note: Implementations MAY return UNSPECIFIED_DENY instead where disclosing a sanctions nexus is itself restricted.

codes.description: Awaiting the off-chain VASP-to-VASP Travel Rule exchange.
Sender or receiver account frozen or deny-listed.
Mint/burn/transfer violates the declared supply model, or insufficient units.
Units are held as a leg of a Committed settlement instruction.
Denied, with no further detail at check time.
